newsitem.title: USA: Checkpoint, Ultrak deal valued at $397 mln. [CORRECTED 01:45 GMT, 12/03].
newsitem.headline: Checkpoint, Ultrak deal valued at $397 mln. [CORRECTED 01:45 GMT, 12/03].

text.p: Wall Street arbitrage traders said a deal in which Checkpoint Systems Inc would merge with Ultrak Inc would be worth about $397 million.
(Corrects value of deal in headline and text from $365 mln).

The companies said late Tuesday they signed a definitive agreement to merge in a stock swap to create a worldwide electronic security and surveillance solutions provider with market capitalization of about $1.3 billion.
"They are both big in security," one arbitrage trader said.

"Ultrak is more closed circuit television systems and Checkpoint is more into the electronic tags in retail stores," the trader added. "This should be very straightforward. I don't see anthing lurking beneath the surface."

The companies said the merger, in which each Ultrak common share would be exchanged for 1.15 Checkpoint common shares, had been apporved by both their boards. The deal is expected to be tax-free and close by mid-1997, they added.

"My initial reaction is that this deal makes the combined entity more competitive in providing the full solutions that retailers want," said one analyst who follows Checkpoint and asked his name not be used. He said he would spend a "long night" analyzing the transaction.
The companies have scheduled a conference call for 11:00 EST Wednesday.

Checkpoint makes electronic surveillance devices, such as radio frequency labels that are installed in products like compact disks when the disks are made. The company also makes sensing systems to detect those labels.
Ultrak makes eight different surveillance products, including closed circut television monitors used in banks and casinos.

Checkpoint's Steven Selfridge, who will be the chief operating officer of the new company, said the merger enables Checkpoint to diversify its product offerings and distribution channels. He said Checkpoint will divest its own circut television unit, Alarmex, as a result of the deal.
Selfridge also said the deal will not be dilutive to the new company's earnings in 1997. It will be accretive in 1998, he added.

Checkpoint may issue up to 17.2 million shares of stock for the transaction, he also said. Checkpoint's shareholders will own about 72 percent of the new company's shares, while Ultrak's shareholders will own about 28 percent.
Ultrak officials were not immediately available to comment further.
The merger still depends on regulatory approval, as well as approval from the shareholders of both companies.
-- Jeff Mamera and Brendan Intindola in the New York newsroom (212) 859-1700
